covers.quote: Don’t overuse text boxes or callouts: they become a distraction.

rules.quote: Limit the use of text boxes and callouts
rules.specification: The page gives no numerical limit or operational test for when boxes and callouts become a distraction.
rules.violation_condition: Text boxes or callouts occur so frequently that they distract from the body text.
rules.why: G-4: the body restates the heading's limit; retain one rule rather than flagging excessive use twice.

rules.quote: Avoid putting content in a text box or callout just because you can’t make it fit into the flow of the text.
rules.specification: The restriction concerns the reason for placement. That reason cannot reliably be established from the finished text alone.
rules.violation_condition: Content has been placed in a text box or callout solely because it could not be fitted into the flow of the text.
rules.why: The placement restriction is distinct from excessive frequency and from the requirement that boxes contain supporting material.

covers.quote: Text boxes should contain a summary, examples or an expansion of ideas in the body of the text.
Use text boxes to set information apart from the content.
You can use text boxes for information that is useful but not part of the main content, for example:
They also make it clear that it shouldn’t be read as part of the main text.

rules.quote: Use text boxes for supporting content, not main text
rules.violation_condition: A text box contains part of the main reading sequence rather than material that supports or supplements it.
when: Supporting material may summarise, exemplify or expand ideas in the body text.
Permitted uses include summaries, checklists, examples, case studies, quotes, links to related information and definitions.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: the descriptions and permitted uses elaborate one supporting-versus-main-content distinction.

rules.quote: Longer text boxes should have a heading or title to show people the purpose of the text box at a glance.
rules.specification: The page does not define how long a text box must be before this requirement applies.
rules.violation_condition: A longer text box lacks a heading or title identifying its purpose.
when: Applies to longer text boxes, not necessarily every text box.
rules.why: G-2: length limits when the heading requirement applies; no unsupported length threshold has been introduced.

covers.quote: You can use an appropriate identifier, such as ‘Box 1’ or ‘Case study 1’.

rules.quote: Number text boxes if they feature repeatedly in content.
rules.specification: The page does not quantify ‘repeatedly’. A recurrence threshold would need to be agreed before implementing an automatic check.
rules.violation_condition: Recurring text boxes lack identifying numbers.
when: Applies when text boxes feature repeatedly in the content.
An appropriate identifier may be used, such as ‘Box 1’ or ‘Case study 1’; neither label is mandatory.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: recurrence triggers numbering, while the identifier wording is a permitted implementation rather than another rule.

rules.quote: Refer to numbered text boxes in the body text.
rules.violation_condition: A numbered text box has no reference to it in the body text.
rules.why: The missing body reference is a different finding from a missing box number, so the two instructions remain separate.

rules.quote: Organise content in a clear order using section headings.
rules.specification: Whether the order is clear requires contextual assessment; the page does not prescribe a particular section sequence.
rules.violation_condition: Web content lacks section-heading structure that makes its organisation and reading order clear.
when: Stated as an accessibility fundamental in the HTML section.
rules.why: This instruction concerns textual organisation through headings, unlike the neighbouring visual-design and device requirements.
